title: Transformer-FSQ: Discrete Latents for Extreme KV-Cache Compression
summary: The method replaces standard key and value projections with a finite scalar quantisation (FSQ) bottleneck, storing packed discrete integer codes per token instead of full-precision KV entries, with no per-token quantisation metadata. Converting a pretrained transformer requires training only the new projections on roughly 0.25 tokens per original parameter, plus adoption of a custom fused Triton decoding kernel. Accuracy can degrade outside the evaluated retrieval setting: the paper shows existing baselines fail beyond moderate ratios, and the method's gains are demonstrated on RULER long-context retrieval for Qwen-family base models 0.6B-8B, not on general generation quality or instruction-tuned chat workloads.
rationale: Although the compression ratios directly address the reader's single-24GB-GPU constraint and conversion cost is low, the technique requires modifying a model's projection layers, running a short training conversion, and depending on a custom kernel with accuracy validated only on retrieval benchmarks, so it merits tracking and small-scale experimentation rather than immediate production adoption.

claims.statement: The method replaces standard key and value projections with a finite scalar quantisation (FSQ) bottleneck, storing packed discrete integer codes per token instead of full-precision KV entries, with no per-token quantisation metadata. Converting a pretrained transformer requires training only the new projections on roughly 0.25 tokens per original parameter, plus adoption of a custom fused Triton decoding kernel. Accuracy can degrade outside the evaluated retrieval setting: the paper shows existing baselines fail beyond moderate ratios, and the method's gains are demonstrated on RULER long-context retrieval for Qwen-family base models 0.6B-8B, not on general generation quality or instruction-tuned chat workloads.

The method stores the KV cache as packed integer codes achieving 12x to 97.5x compression; it is the most accurate method evaluated on RULER across that range, and its fused Triton kernel decodes at 1.01x native SDPA throughput at 32x compression and 1.54x at 97.5x on Qwen3-8B-Base.
